title: Lost in Delegation: Studying the Effectiveness of Task Orchestration in Generative Search
abstract: arXiv:2611.16526v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLMs have quickly evolved from models used in isolation to agentic systems that delegate tasks to external tools and other LLMs to solve complex assignments. This agentic augmentation has led to impressive capability gains. However, when and how delegation improves performance remains poorly understood. For example, it is unclear whether delegation helps when tasks involve post-cutoff information that the orchestrating LLM cannot reliably resolve from its own knowledge. In this work, we use purpose-built datasets with pre- and post-cutoff splits to compare various delegation modes. We find that delegation provides no consistent accuracy improvement over non-delegated setups, with effects varying across models and tasks. When tasks involve knowledge unavailable to the orchestrator, delegation can substantially degrade accuracy, while direct tool use with the same LLM performs much better. Our analysis identifies distorted delegated querie

translated_title: 委派中的迷失：研究生成式搜索中任务编排的有效性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）已从单独使用的模型迅速演变为能够将任务委派给外部工具和其他LLM以解决复杂任务的智能体系统。这种智能体式增强带来了令人瞩目的能力提升。然而，委派在何时以及如何提升性能仍然缺乏深入理解。例如，当任务涉及编排LLM无法从自身知识中可靠解决的截止日期后信息时，委派是否有帮助尚不清楚。在这项工作中，我们使用专门构建的、带有截止日期前/后划分的数据集来比较各种委派模式。我们发现，与非委派设置相比，委派并不能带来一致的准确性提升，其效果因模型和任务而异。当任务涉及编排模型无法获取的知识时，委派可能大幅降低准确性，而使用同一个LLM直接调用工具的表现要好得多。我们的分析识别出失真的委派查询（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 本研究通过专门的截止日期前后数据集系统比较多种任务委派模式，发现LLM间的任务委派并不总能带来准确性提升——当任务涉及编排模型未知的信息时，委派反而会显著降低准确性，而直接进行工具调用的效果要好得多。
en_tdlr: This study uses purpose-built pre- and post-cutoff datasets to compare various delegation modes, finding that LLM task delegation does not consistently improve accuracy and can substantially degrade performance when tasks involve knowledge unavailable to the orchestrating LLM, while direct tool use performs much better.
